items.caption:
I found this video from almost 5 years ago 🤯 but I still remember this moment like it happened yesterday. 

We waited my entire pregnancy to find out if our first baby was a boy or a girl.

And in my head, I had definitely built up this movie-worthy moment where the baby would be born, someone would yell “IT’S A ___!” and we’d both burst into tears. 😂

Except… that’s not what happened at all.

She was born, they put her on my chest, and for probably the first 15 minutes we genuinely had NO idea whether we had a son or a daughter. And we didn’t care. 😂

We were looking at her face, talking to her, soaking in the fact that there was suddenly an actual HUMAN lying on my chest after all those months of wondering who was in there.

Eventually one of the nurses was basically like… “Wait, is it a girl or boy?” Oh. Right. 😂 I looked and it was A GIRL! 

But I remember being surprised by how uneventful that part felt. 👆

Not because we weren’t excited to have a daughter — we obviously were — but because in that moment, “boy or girl” suddenly felt so much smaller than I had imagined it would.

Did you find out during pregnancy or wait until birth? And if you waited… was the reveal as dramatic as you imagined it would be? 😂

#pregnancy #pregnant #birth #naturalbirth #relatablemom

And then finally they were like filling out the forms and they asked and we were like, oh, and we looked and it was a girl. But to be honest, it was pretty uneventful because we didn't care either way. We were just so happy to have this happy baby.

items.caption:
My husband is scared that having a third baby could be a mistake.And the weirdest part is… I understand that fear more than he probably realizes.

When I was pregnant with our second, I remember genuinely wondering if we had made a mistake too.

I loved our daughter SO much that I could not wrap my head around how another baby could possibly fit into our family without changing everything I loved about it.

I worried I wouldn’t love him the same. I worried he would never “live up” to the relationship I already had with her. And even at 8 months pregnant, I was still having those thoughts.

Then he was born. And of course, now I look at him and cannot imagine our family without him.

But I also don’t think that means every fear about having another baby should automatically be dismissed with “you’ll never regret the baby once they’re here.”

Because deciding whether to have a third feels different.

We already love our life. We love our family dynamic. We know how much another baby would change our time, energy, finances, routines, travel… basically everything.

So lately my husband and I have been having some really deep conversations about what we actually want our family to look like.

I’m curious though — if you have 3+ kids, did you feel completely sure before trying for another… or did you have a lot of fear too?

#relatablemom #relatablemotherhood #momsofinstagram #pregnant #babynumber3

items.caption:
9 cm dilated with my first baby and completely unmedicated. And somehow… I still felt incredibly calm and confident in what my body was doing. 🤍

I share my births because I think women deserve to see more examples of birth that aren’t centered around fear.

That doesn’t mean I believe everyone needs to have an unmedicated birth.

I believe women deserve to understand their options, know what questions to ask, make a birth plan, build a support system they trust, and walk into birth feeling like an active participant in their care — not like birth is just something that happens to them.

Before my first birth, I spent so much time learning about labor, interventions, pain management, positioning, advocacy, and what I wanted my birth environment to feel like.

Did everything go exactly according to plan? Of course not. But having a plan wasn’t about controlling every detail.

It was about knowing my preferences, understanding my options, and feeling confident enough to make decisions when things changed. And honestly, that philosophy has carried into so much of motherhood for me. I don’t want someone else to tell me what I’m supposed to do.

I want good information.
I want to understand my options.
I want to ask questions.
And then I want to feel confident making the decision that works best for my family.

If that sounds like you too, come hang out on my page. 🤍

I share a lot more birth footage like this, pregnancy + postpartum, motherhood, and everything I’m learning along the way as I try to make informed decisions for my family without feeling like I have to do motherhood exactly like everyone else.

And if you’re pregnant right now, I have a free unmedicated birth guide plus more resources linked in my bio to help you feel more prepared going into birth.

Follow along — there’s a lot more coming. 🤍

items.caption:
One of the coolest things about labor is realizing just how much your body is doing behind the scenes. 🤯

During unmedicated labor, your body releases hormones like oxytocin and endorphins that help you cope with contractions — and for some women, that can create this incredibly relaxed, floaty, almost euphoric feeling between them.

This was me 😂 Completely in my own little world.

And I think this is something we don’t talk about enough.

Birth is so often portrayed as something terrifying that happens to you, when in reality, your body has some pretty incredible systems designed to help you through it.

That doesn’t mean birth is painless. It doesn’t mean every labor looks like this. And there is absolutely no “right” way to give birth.

But I wish more women went into birth knowing what their bodies are capable of instead of only hearing everything that could go wrong.

Follow along for more positive, empowering birth education + real-life motherhood 🤍

#positivebirth #unmedicatedbirth #birthstory #naturalbirth #naturalbirthing

items.caption:
I remember this contraction so vividly.

We were only about two hours into labor, and I remember thinking, “There is absolutely no way I can keep doing this for hours.”

It already felt so intense. And because I had no idea how much longer I had left, my brain immediately went to: If this is where we are now… how am I possibly going to make it to the end?

What I didn’t know was that I was already so much closer to meeting my baby than I realized. That’s one of the hardest parts of labor—you don’t get a countdown clock. You don’t always know if you have 20 minutes left or 10 hours.

Sometimes the moment you start thinking “I can’t do this anymore” is the exact moment you need to stop thinking about the rest of labor entirely.

Focus on the moment that you’re in. Breathe through this one. Relax your body through this one. Let this one pass. And then you do it again.

You don’t have to feel fearless to be powerful in birth. You can doubt yourself. You can say you can’t do it. You can feel overwhelmed by the intensity… and still keep going.

Your body can be doing something incredibly powerful even while your mind is questioning whether you’re capable of it.

I wish every mom going into birth knew that having a moment of “I can’t” doesn’t mean you’re failing. Sometimes it means you’re right in the middle of doing something you never knew you were strong enough to do. 🤍
